# 📜 Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct for Sovereign AI Researchers & Developers

**Version**: 2.1 Adapted for Zoth Studio & Sovereign AI Research  
**Applies to**: All project spaces, repositories, issue trackers, discussions, and sovereign comms channels.

---

## 🌟 1. Our Pledge

We as members, contributors, and maintainers of the **Zoth Studio** project pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free, welcoming, and intellectually rigorous experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, mathematically rigorous, and privacy-respecting sovereign development collective.

---

## 🧭 2. Our Standards

### Positive Behaviors:
- **Championing Privacy & User Sovereignty**: Prioritizing zero-cloud egress, local-first computing, and cryptographic protections across all toolchains and interfaces.
- **Mathematical & Scientific Rigor**: Grounding architectural discussions, consensus mechanisms, and visual algorithms in demonstrable mathematics, formal theory, and empirical benchmarks.
- **Constructive & Thoughtful Collaboration**: Providing clear, actionable, and empathetic feedback on pull requests, RFCs, and code audits.
- **Respecting Operator Autonomy**: Honoring the user's absolute ownership over their hardware, private keys, cognitive memory engrams, and agent swarms.
- **Graceful Error Handling**: Treating software bugs, performance bottlenecks, and divergent perspectives as opportunities for iterative improvement.

### Unacceptable Behaviors:
- **Telemetry or Backdoor Injection**: Introducing unauthorized tracking beacons, covert telemetry, phone-home telemetry calls, analytics scrapers, or cryptographic backdoors.
- **De-anonymization & Doxxing**: Publishing or threatening to publish private identifying information (PII), physical locations, or personal credentials without explicit consent.
- **Harassment & Trolling**: The use of sexualized language or imagery, unwelcome sexual attention or advances, insulting/derogatory comments, personal or political attacks, and deliberate disruption.
- **Hostile Code Submissions**: Submitting deliberately obfuscated malicious payloads, unverified dependency supply chain attacks, or weaponized exploits into the public workspace.
- **Other Unprofessional Conduct**: Any conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate or destructive in a professional, collaborative environment.

---

## 🛡️ 3. Enforcement Responsibilities

Community maintainers are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned with this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

---

## 🌐 4. Scope

This Code of Conduct applies within all project spaces (GitHub repositories, issue trackers, pull requests, discussions, and release pipelines), and also applies when an individual is officially representing the project in public spaces or sovereign relays (e.g., SimpleX channels, technical symposia, or conferences).

---

## ⚖️ 5. Enforcement Guidelines

When a violation of this Code of Conduct is reported, maintainers will follow these enforcement guidelines:

### 1. Correction
- **Community Impact**: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.
- **Consequence**: A private, written warning from maintainers, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. An apology may be requested.

### 2. Warning
- **Community Impact**: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.
- **Consequence**: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in project spaces as well as external channels like social media.

### 3. Temporary Suspension
- **Community Impact**: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, telemetry insertion, or targeted harassment.
- **Consequence**: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the project community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved is allowed during this period.

### 4. Permanent Ban
- **Community Impact**: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained harassment, doxxing, malicious backdoor deployment, or overt aggression.
- **Consequence**: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the project community.

---

## 📬 6. Reporting & Contact

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the project leadership at:
- **Email**: `conduct@nullai.tech`
- **Private E2EE Channel**: Via the SimpleX Sovereign Bridge (`zoth simplex`)

All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly. Maintainers are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

---

## 📜 7. Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org), version 2.1, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html, with specialized adaptations for sovereign AI research, zero-telemetry computing, and local-first software development.
